TEN-1.title: Tenant comes from the credential only
TEN-1.mechanism: `TenantScopeMiddleware` reads `tenant_id` from the JWT only; `EndpointSpineTests` bans tenant route/query params; `ContractShapeTests` bans `TenantId` on requests

TEN-2.title: Ambient scope, fail-closed
TEN-2.note: the non-HTTP job base class is owed (trigger: first background job)

TEN-4.title: Save-time guard and write provenance
TEN-4.mechanism: `KernelDbContext.GuardTenancy` on both SaveChanges variants; `TenantGuardTests`; integration cross-tenant modify; `BulkWriteBanTests` bans the write paths that bypass the save pipeline (EF set-based, raw SQL, raw ADO)
TEN-4.note: the write-provenance stamps are owed (trigger: next edition build pass); the tenancy guard is what is proven here

TEN-5.title: Sanctioned-bypass ledger
TEN-5.mechanism: `docs/claims/tenant-bypass-ledger.md` (empty) + docs-lint rule that a row without a sole-reader test fails
TEN-5.note: ledger empty; the first sanctioned bypass is its first run

TEN-6.title: Tenant is minted from membership, never asserted
TEN-6.note: trigger: first identity slice (shared with SEC-4's version store and SEC-10)

SEC-1.title: Every endpoint gated
SEC-1.mechanism: deny-by-default fallback policy + cached `PermissionPolicyProvider`; `EndpointSpineTests` asserts the fallback denies, allowlists `/health`, and requires a permission policy per endpoint; the `sv`/tenant gates run after routing and exempt allowlisted-anonymous endpoints

SEC-2.title: Anti mass-assignment
SEC-2.mechanism: `ContractShapeTests` forbidden-field registry; `EndpointSpineTests` scans every body-bound DTO for server fields, nested and immutable constructor-bound DTOs included; App/Api declare no request/response types

SEC-3.title: No PII in URLs
SEC-3.mechanism: `EndpointSpineTests` route + query scan ([AsParameters] wrappers, collections, DateTime/TimeOnly)

SEC-4.title: JWT hardening and revocation
SEC-4.mechanism: pinned HS256, `RequireSignedTokens`, `SessionVersionMiddleware`; `HostSecurityTests` rejects a wrong-algorithm token and a missing-sv token
SEC-4.note: EF-backed session store owed (trigger: first identity slice)

SEC-5.title: No secrets in config
SEC-5.mechanism: `UserSecretsId` + `SecretConfigShapeTests` over every committed JSON config under `src/` + the CI secret-scan job
SEC-5.note: vault-port interface owed (trigger: first runtime credential)

SEC-6.title: Log safety
SEC-6.note: v1 surfaces tested; hub log-safety owed (trigger: realtime)

SEC-7.title: Opaque public identifiers
SEC-7.note: trigger: the first anonymous resource surface in an edition project (the kernel exemplar has none)

SEC-8.title: Abuse posture
SEC-8.note: trigger: the first publicly exposed edition host (the launch pre-flight names it)

SEC-9.title: Deployment-edge hardening
SEC-9.note: trigger: the first deployed edition host (arrives with the launch pre-flight)

SEC-10.title: Authentication strength asserted at mint, verified at the gate
SEC-10.note: trigger: first identity slice (shared with SEC-4's version store and TEN-6)

SEC-11.title: The runtime credential cannot touch the schema
SEC-11.note: trigger: the next edition build pass (rides DATA-6: the migrate mode and the role split are one provisioning story; the integration tier's provisioning path is where both roles are created)

TIME-1.title: UTC, offset-aware, and nothing else
TIME-1.mechanism: `TimeTypeTests` over Contracts, App, Persistence (recurses Nullable, arrays, generics)
TIME-1.note: DB UTC column defaults not used: the service sets the value

DATA-1.title: Stores, records, downward deps
DATA-1.mechanism: layer references + `DependencyDirectionTests`; one service call per endpoint

DATA-2.title: Bounded reads
DATA-2.mechanism: `EfNoteStore` AsNoTracking + `(CreatedAtUtc, Id)` keyset + the shared page-size clamp; `NoteServiceTests`, integration `KeysetPagingTests` incl. a same-timestamp collision page
DATA-2.note: structural + review; single module, no shared store base

DATA-3.title: Two-layer at-most-once
DATA-3.note: trigger: first idempotent external side effect

DATA-5.title: Fail-fast mandatory config
DATA-5.mechanism: `Required()` startup reads; `StartupConfigTests` fails per missing key

DATA-6.title: Migrate and exit
DATA-6.note: trigger: the next edition build pass (a small host change; the mechanism is two facts on the composed host)

DATA-7.title: Ruled retention and disposal
DATA-7.note: trigger: the first PII-bearing entity in an edition project, or the first contractual deletion clause, whichever lands first

DATA-8.title: A state change and its event commit together or not at all
DATA-8.note: trigger: the first event publish in an edition project (arrives with the first broker, alongside RES-5)

DATA-9.title: A stale write is refused, never silently applied
DATA-9.note: trigger: the next edition build pass (rides TEN-4's interceptor work; the token and the refusal live in the same save pipeline the tenancy guard already owns)

DATA-10.title: Everything that grows has a registered sweep
DATA-10.note: trigger: the first append-only operational table in an edition project (DATA-8's outbox is the likely first, with RES-5's dead-letter quarantine close behind)

DATA-11.title: A migration never breaks the release running beside it
DATA-11.note: trigger: the first production deployment with rolling replacement; the lint half can land at the next edition build pass, ahead of the compatibility job

CFG-1.title: Operational settings are configuration, not code
CFG-1.mechanism: `OperationalSettingsTests` scans `server/src` and `scripts/` for model-id and provider-endpoint literals; `scripts/e2e.sh` reads Jwt values from committed appsettings, never duplicating them

CON-1.title: One wire dialect
CON-1.mechanism: ProblemDetails + StatusCodePages + single camelCase enum converter; `WireConventionTests` (naming, enum round-trip, problem+json)

CON-2.title: Contract parity fixture
CON-2.mechanism: shared `note-contract.fixture.json` linked into C# tests + read by the TS test; `ContractParityTests`, `noteContract.test.ts`

CON-3.title: Read completeness for action-bearing surfaces
CON-3.note: trigger: the first edition project with a restorable session (the kernel exemplar has none)

CON-4.title: A breaking change is detected by machine, approved by human
CON-4.note: trigger: the first published external contract (a versioned API consumed outside the repo, a partner surface, or the first schema registry; the composed client in the same repo is CON-2's territory, not a published contract)

RT-1.title: Realtime discipline
RT-1.note: trigger: first realtime slice; the promotion set is the hub arch test, MaximumReceiveMessageSize, the createHub client seam, and the socket harness scenario

SRV-1.title: One deployable unit
SRV-1.note: trigger: the next edition build pass. Applies to web products; an API-only project re-rules it in its deltas file at adoption

RES-1.title: Every outbound call is bounded, and retries are earned
RES-1.note: trigger: the first external service dependency in an edition project. Database session bounds are RES-6's, carved out so this claim stays about the chokepoint shape

RES-2.title: No unbounded queue, pool, or backlog in the process
RES-2.note: trigger: the first background worker or in-process queue in an edition project

RES-3.title: The host dies cleanly, and there is a test that kills it
RES-3.note: trigger: the first deployed edition host (rides SEC-9's deployment-edge work; the drain budget is a CFG-1 operational setting ruled against the platform's grace period)

RES-4.title: Liveness answers alone; readiness answers for its dependencies
RES-4.note: trigger: the first deployed edition host (lands with RES-3 and SEC-9; the health root SEC-1 already allowlists is the surface this claim splits in two)

RES-5.title: Poison is quarantined at a counted limit, never retried forever, never dropped
RES-5.note: trigger: the first message broker in an edition project (the transactional outbox relay, DATA-8, is the likely first consumer)

RES-6.title: Every database session carries four finite bounds, each proven where it lives
RES-6.note: trigger: the next edition build pass. Everything here runs on the existing integration tier against the real engine, so proven is reachable immediately; nothing waits on a new dependency

PERF-1.title: A hot operation's IO is counted, budgeted, and gated
PERF-1.note: trigger: the next edition build pass (the v1 exemplar's list endpoint is the first designated seam; the interceptor rides the same seam TEN-4's stamps use)

PERF-2.title: A designated hot path's allocations are budgeted per operation
PERF-2.note: trigger: the first designated hot path in an edition project; designation before need fails the YAGNI gate, so the family expects most projects to hold zero designations for a long time, honestly

PERF-3.title: A designated algorithmic seam proves its scaling with a counted ratio
PERF-3.note: trigger: the first hand-written algorithm over unbounded input in an edition project; library calls and database queries are not designations (the library's complexity is its documentation's promise, and query shape is PERF-1's and DATA-2's)

PERF-4.title: No sync IO and no whole-payload buffering on the serving path
PERF-4.note: trigger: the next edition build pass (a BannedApiAnalyzers configuration plus one host assertion; the client side already carries the idiom under UI-2's lint discipline)

PERF-5.title: Every cache is bounded and every entry expires
PERF-5.note: trigger: the first cache in an edition project; the claim deliberately does not mandate caching anywhere, it prices caching where chosen

PERF-6.title: Wall time is never asserted raw
PERF-6.note: trigger: the first wall-time benchmark in an edition project; the lint half can land at the next edition build pass, ahead of any benchmark existing, since its job is to keep the first timing assert out

MOD-1.title: Module co-location
MOD-1.mechanism: Notes module co-located; client deep-path import bans
MOD-1.note: single module; the cross-module rules have no second module to constrain, so the second module is their first real run

DOC-1.title: Documentation lifecycle
DOC-1.mechanism: `docs-lint.mjs`: front matter, placement, work slice ids, the narrow design/ governance, the MET-08 dash check (exclusions declared above)
DOC-1.note: forward-only status transitions not linted, stateless

DEC-1.title: A module's behaviour traces to a decision
DEC-1.mechanism: docs-lint fails a `docs/decisions/*.md` without a `provenance` field (the upward link); the decision template models the field
DEC-1.note: the downward link is owed (trigger: first regeneration of a module from its decisions); the artifact-order check rides here too (trigger: next acceptance test); the upward provenance lint is built and proven

UI-1.title: Token source lockstep
UI-1.mechanism: `tokenCoverage.test.ts` reads the export at its canonical home `design/prototype/_ds/colors_and_type.css` (every CSS var has a token, count > 50)

UI-2.title: Literal visual values are lint errors
UI-2.mechanism: `eslint.config.js` bans visual literals in styles: colors, font props, radii, hairlines, and spacing/dimension literals (numerics matched on `raw`), with the structural allowlist

UI-3.title: Screens compose primitives only
UI-3.mechanism: `Text`/`Button` are the only token importers (eslint no-restricted-imports + naming scan)

UI-4.title: Fidelity ledger
UI-4.note: each screen owes its suite; per-atom resolved-style assertions not included; the prototype-to-ledger exporter owed

UI-5.title: Thin UI over tested services, composed entrypoint exercised
UI-5.mechanism: eslint bans `api/**` and `data/**` imports outside the composition root (`src/main.tsx`); `npm run smoke` boots the ACTUAL `src/main.tsx` in jsdom against the live server, asserting a real GET and a real POST; runs in the CI e2e job and `scripts/e2e.sh`
UI-5.note: the import ban is proven-centralized; each new primary flow owes its smoke line

DEP-1.title: Dependency quarantine
DEP-1.mechanism: CPM exact pins + lockfiles + locked-mode restore (`--locked-mode` / `npm ci`) + `VERSIONS.md` (90-day window header, container-images section, kernel-provenance section) + docs-lint ledger, image, and kernel-provenance checks; the SQL Server image is one tag@digest value across runbook, CI, and the Testcontainers fixture
DEP-1.note: publish-date CI check owed (dates recorded by hand); kernel-provenance check latent until the next instantiation fills a real pin

DEP-2.title: Standing advisory sweep with a remediation clock
DEP-2.note: trigger: the first armed CI loop (TEST-3 at instantiation); the publish-date check DEP-1 names as its upgrade path rides the same job

TEST-1.title: Tier strategy
TEST-1.mechanism: SQLite unit/arch, Testcontainers integration; EF InMemory banned by `NamingPlacementTests`

TEST-2.title: E2E harness
TEST-2.mechanism: `tools/harness/main.ts` drives the real client services (NDJSON + redaction, fails loudly not vacuously); the completeness self-audit fails on any undriven repo method; the gated harness profile refuses outside Development/Testing (`HarnessProfileTests`)
TEST-2.note: the harness-profile gate is latent: there is no product-owned provider port to re-bind yet, so the first one is its first re-binding

TEST-3.title: CI loop
TEST-3.note: mechanism built, not yet armed: branch protection is set at instantiation; until then the loop blocks nothing

TEST-4.title: Real-runtime boot proof
TEST-4.note: trigger: the next edition build pass. UI-5's composed smoke already proves entrypoint wiring in-process; the real-boot script assertion and built-form pinning are the promotion set that completes it

HUM-1.title: Irreversible surfaces get a human turn, unconditionally
HUM-1.mechanism: `.github/CODEOWNERS` covers migrations, contracts, and `docs/contracts/` (`@OWNER` renamed at instantiation); docs-lint fails if any of the three loses its owned entry; branch protection requires code-owner review
HUM-1.note: mechanism built, not yet armed: it arms with TEST-3 at instantiation; the manifest carries the step

AI-1.title: Server-injected identity
AI-1.mechanism: `ToolExecutor` reject-then-inject + throw-on-unset, rejecting server-owned keys recursively through nested objects and lists; `ToolExecutorTests` incl. a nested-payload case
AI-1.note: nested dictionaries/lists stripped; `JsonElement`-typed nesting remains a per-tool review item

AI-2.title: Untrusted content, no authority
AI-2.note: the v1 tool has its guard test, each new tool owes its own; full taint tracking and the SSRF egress guard are owed (trigger: outbound agentic requests)

AI-3.title: Prompt architecture
AI-3.note: trigger: the first model-backed feature in an edition project

OBS-1.title: External-effect seam observability
OBS-1.note: trigger: the first external side-effect port in an edition project. This claim opens the observability family the v1 cut deliberately deferred

OBS-2.title: Refusals and privileged actions are security events
OBS-2.note: trigger: the first deployed edition host (alongside SEC-9; the refusal seams it instruments are already built and tested, so the events attach to existing tested paths)
